newsitem.title: INDIA: India campaigner marks anniversary with balloon.
newsitem.headline: India campaigner marks anniversary with balloon.

text.p: A tall balloon in the shape of India's national emblem arose next to New Delhi's Parliament House on Thursday evening as thousands of Indians began a march to celebrate a half-century of independence.

"This is specially designed and fabricated for the 50th year," former lawmaker Vishwa Bandhu Gupta, 70, told Reuters as dozens of workers pumped in cold helium to erect the 100-foot (30.5-metre) balloon.

The emblem, first used by Buddhist Emperor Ashoka over 2,000 years ago, shows four lions standing back-to-back, three of them visible at a time. At the base are images of a bull and a horse symbolising the movement of life.
India adopted the emblem as a national symbol when it won freedom from British rule in 1947. The wheel in the emblem forms the centre of India's saffron, white and green flag.
"I was standing here 50 years ago," Gupta, who took part in India's independence movement, said outside the huge, circular parliament building.
